title: Massage After Surfing: Sore Shoulders, Back and Neck
excerpt: Why surfing leaves your shoulders, back and neck sore, which massage helps after a surf, when to book it, and when to see a doctor instead.
content_html:
After a surf, most of the soreness sits in the shoulders, upper back, neck and lower back, because paddling does most of the work. A sports massage or a deep tissue massage suits muscles that feel tight and worked, and a lighter massage suits a body that is simply tired. The best time is usually the evening after the session or the next day, when the soreness has had time to show.

Why surfing makes you sore

Most of a surf is spent paddling, not riding waves. You lie on your stomach with your chest lifted and your head up, and pull through the water with your arms, again and again. That position works muscles many people rarely use for that long, which is why the first few days of a surf trip often leave you stiff the next morning.

This kind of next-day stiffness is called delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS). It usually starts 12 to 24 hours after unfamiliar or long exercise, is worst at around 24 to 72 hours, and fades within a few days.

Does massage help sore muscles after surfing?

For soreness, it can. A 2018 review in Frontiers in Physiology compared recovery methods after exercise and found massage to be one of the most effective for reducing muscle soreness and the feeling of fatigue. The effect is modest, and it is about how your muscles feel, not about making you stronger or preventing injury.

Massage does not repair a strained muscle, and it is no substitute for rest, water, food and sleep. What it can do is ease stiffness, help you relax after a long day in the water and make the next session feel less sluggish.

If you are not sure, a sports massage is the usual choice after surfing. Tell your therapist that you surf and which areas feel worst; most surfers ask for the shoulders, upper back and neck first. For the difference between firm styles, see Swedish vs deep tissue massage.

When to book a massage after surfing

  • The same evening: a good time for a relaxing or medium-pressure massage, once you have showered, eaten and had some water.

  • The next day: when soreness usually shows, so firmer work on specific areas often feels most useful then.

  • Before a surf: keep it light and short. Very firm pressure just before paddling can leave muscles feeling heavy.

  • On a surf trip: many surfers book one massage after the first two or three days, when the shoulders have taken the most, and another before the flight home.

For how often a massage makes sense over a longer stay, see how often should you get a massage.

Tell your therapist about your skin

A day of surfing is hard on skin as well as muscle. Before your massage, mention:

  • Sunburn: firm pressure on sunburnt skin hurts and can make it worse. Ask for the area to be avoided, or choose a gentle aloe vera treatment until it settles.

  • Reef cuts and grazes: keep oil and pressure away from them until they have closed. Coral cuts can become infected, so keep them clean and see a doctor if one becomes red, hot or swollen.

  • Rash from the board or wax: usually on the chest, stomach or inner thighs; the therapist can work around it.

Simple stretches between surfs

These are gentle stretches for the areas paddling uses most. Hold each for about 30 seconds, breathe slowly and stop if anything hurts.

  • Chest: stand in a doorway with your forearms on the frame and lean forward until you feel a stretch across the chest.

  • Upper back: kneel, sit back on your heels and reach your arms forward along the floor (child's pose).

  • Neck: sitting tall, tip one ear towards your shoulder, then change sides.

  • Hips: kneel on one knee with the other foot in front, and move your hips gently forward.

  • Calves: stand with your hands on a wall, one leg back with the heel down.

When to see a doctor instead

Normal soreness after surfing is a dull ache that eases within a few days. See a doctor or physiotherapist rather than booking a massage if you have:

  • Sharp pain, or pain that is getting worse after three or four days

  • A shoulder you cannot lift, or one that clicks and hurts

  • Numbness or tingling in an arm or hand

  • Swelling, bruising or a joint that gives way after a wipeout

  • Neck pain after hitting the bottom or being hit by a board

Frequently asked questions

Why do my shoulders hurt after surfing?

Paddling uses the shoulders more than anything else in surfing. Hundreds of strokes in one session, often more than the muscles are used to, leave them tired and sore the next day, especially on the first days of a trip.

Why does my lower back hurt after surfing?

When you paddle, you hold your chest up off the board, and your lower back muscles keep that arch for as long as you are lying down. After a long session they can ache. Breaks to sit on the board and a few stretches afterwards help.

Is it better to have a massage before or after surfing?

After, for most people. A firm massage just before paddling can leave muscles feeling heavy. If you want one before, keep it light and short.

Should I get a sports or a deep tissue massage after surfing?

A sports massage suits recovery between surfs and focuses on the areas you have worked. A deep tissue massage suits tightness that keeps coming back, such as the same knot between the shoulder blades. Both use firm pressure, and you can ask for it lighter.

How long does soreness after surfing last?

Muscle soreness from exercise usually peaks one to three days after the session and fades within about five days. It gets less noticeable as your body gets used to paddling, which is why the first days of a surf trip are often the worst.

Can I surf the day after a massage?

Yes. Many people find their shoulders and back feel looser the next day. If you had a very firm massage, start with a shorter session.

Can I have a massage with sunburn after surfing?

Not firm massage on the sunburnt areas. Ask your therapist to avoid them, or choose a gentle aloe vera treatment for mild sunburn. Blistered skin needs a doctor, not a massage.
